title: Token economics field interview - NorthForge discovery
header: Date: 2027-01-30; Start: 16:00 UTC; Duration: 48m; Recording: enabled; Location: Zoom
summary: Discovery focused on per-token pricing sensitivity, batching and KV/prefix cache opportunities, and tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for NorthForge's financial data workloads. Customer wants pilot budget of ~ $15k/month and SLA targets ~ <150ms p95 for chat flows. Action: send pilot pricing, security pack, and benchmark plan.
topics: capacity models: hosted vs dedicated vs private
transcript:
00:00 Alice Marsh: hi everyone, thanks for joining. i'm alice from Redwood, AE on this account. appreciate you blocking time. can you, uh, kick off with a quick intro from northforge?
00:12 Lena Park: yeah hi all this is lena head of ai at northforge, uh we build a synthesis and exec summary product for institutional research. Marcus is our CTO, Priya runs infra.
00:22 Marcus Dutta: hey all. our flows are a mix of short prompts (1-2 sentences) and longer summarizations maybe 1-2k tokens per request on some jobs.
00:33 Ben Ortiz: ok that's helpful. what's your traffic shape, like rps and spikes?
00:38 Marcus Dutta: baseline about 8 rps across models, spikes to ~60 rps during market open windows. lots of concurrency but bursty.
00:48 Alice Marsh: thanks. last time we saw similar patterns, batching helps a lot for tailing cost, caching also if you have repeated prefixes. do you have many repeated prompts or templated prompts?
00:58 Lena Park: yes quite a few templates for earnings call templates, we do a lot of prompt-slicing too. about 20% of calls are almost identical with only entity tokens changing.
01:10 Priya Iyer: our constraint is budget. leadership gave us a pilot envelope of $15k/month to prove an ROI before committing to dedicated. also we have strict requirements on data residency and KMS key control.
01:24 Samir Ghosh: that's pretty common. we typically map per-token burn and show where batching + KV cache can reduce unit cost 30-70% depending on repeat rate.
01:36 Lena Park: can you explain the typical numbers? like what does per-token mean end-to-end with streaming?
01:42 Ben Ortiz: sure. with Redwood hosted, per-token billing is for input + output tokens once decoded. streaming doesn't change the per-token calculation, but batching reduces tokens processed per GPU step by packing sequences which amortizes kernel overheads. for a 2k token summary you can see big gains if you can batch several similar-length requests.
02:03 Marcus Dutta: what about KV cache benefits? we do stateful chat with per-user context and reuse history a lot.
02:09 Ben Ortiz: KV cache means we keep key/value cache on the serving node across calls so repeated prefixes don't recompute attention. if you can serve a lot of reuse we can drop compute significantly — but caching works better on Dedicated or Private where you can pin routing, though Hosted also supports prefix caching with smart routing but with some eviction constraints.
02:33 Lena Park: eviction like if you go multi-region?
02:36 Ben Ortiz: yep. routing and cache residency can evict or miss if the request hits a different node. Dedicated gives you more predictable cache hit rates.
02:45 Priya Iyer: ok so quick sanity: pilot 15k/month — can you show a couple of scenarios: hosted with batching/caching vs dedicated minimal node?
02:54 Alice Marsh: absolutely. we usually run a small cost model. as a ballpark, for your mix — short prompts average 120 tokens in/out, long summaries 1.8k tokens. if 70% of traffic is short, 30% long, baseline per-token cost on hosted with standard model is $0.00003 per token input+output (note: example pricing for discussion), which maps to about $12k/month before optimizations. with batching improvements (pack factor ~3) and prefix/KV caching on suitable flows, you could get effective unit cost down 35-45% bringing pilot consumption into your budget comfortably.
03:36 Marcus Dutta: that baseline number — is that list price or our negotiated?
03:39 Alice Marsh: that's public list for hosted, negotiations or committed cadence can go lower; Dedicated has different pricing (node-hour + lower per-token or throughput licensing) that often makes sense at scale.
03:51 Marcus Dutta: timeline: we need to show performance under our real data in 4 weeks. can you run a benchmark?
03:56 Ben Ortiz: yes we can. we'd propose a 2-week benchmark with a small dedicated pool or a hosted pilot with pinned routing to simulate cache behavior. need sample traffic and a few representative prompt sets.
04:08 Lena Park: about security: SOC2 is table stakes, but we need customer-managed KMS for vectors and audit logs. does Redwood Private give us that?
04:17 Samir Ghosh: Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane and on-prem options with KMS integration, yes. Dedicated can also integrate KMS in some setups but Private is the only one that gives full network isolation and air-gap if required.
04:29 Priya Iyer: ok and SSO, RBAC?
04:31 Alice Marsh: we support SAML/SSO, fine-grained RBAC, and token-level auditing in the Console.
04:38 Marcus Dutta: small nit — latency. our SLO target is p95 < 150ms for short chat turn. can you hit that on hosted?
04:46 Ben Ortiz: for short prompts, hosted with lower-level models (e.g., redwood-lite variants) can hit <100ms p95 in many regions. p95 depends on queuing and kernel path. Dedicated often gives more consistent tail latency because you control the pool and autoscaling behavior.
05:02 Lena Park: what about fallback? if a dedicated node is saturated can you fallback to hosted?
05:07 Alice Marsh: yes we support smart routing and fallback policies — you can prefer Dedicated but fallback to Hosted-compatible variant to keep throughput. that impacts cost and potentially slightly different model variant quality — we surface that in the Console.
05:20 Marcus Dutta: how do you model burst pricing and overages?
05:23 Alice Marsh: typically pilot commitments with burst capacity options. for Dedicated we can set burst buckets; for Hosted you can increase quota for a period with surcharge. we'll put concrete numbers in the pricing sheet.
05:34 Priya Iyer: we've seen some transcripts from other vendors where token accounting was opaque; can you provide per-route token breakdown by prompt, by model?
05:43 Samir Ghosh: yes Console gives token-level logs and we can instrument per-route breakdown. we'll share an example export.
05:50 Lena Park: any caveats with your KV cache while using multi-tenant Hosted? we've had issues with cold-starts causing misses during peak.
05:58 Ben Ortiz: fair, cold-starts are a thing. Hosted mitigations: warm pools, prefix-aware routing heuristics, and prewarming triggers. but you get best cache hit rates on Dedicated/Private where you don't move traffic between nodes.
06:12 Marcus Dutta: for the benchmark — we need measures: p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, cost per 1M effective tokens, and cache hit-rate.
06:20 Alice Marsh: that matches our usual deliverables. we'll propose a benchmark plan.
06:24 Priya Iyer: about data residency — our corp legal requires that PII stays in-region EU only. options?
06:31 Samir Ghosh: we have EU-hosted regions and Private deployments that can be deployed into your VPC in region. we'll annotate the security pack with data flow diagrams.
06:43 Lena Park: competition: we looked at CloudX endpoints and FastServe (both), they promised similar batching gains but their prefix cache was limited.
06:50 Alice Marsh: noted. we'll include comparative notes.
06:53 Marcus Dutta: ok so next steps?
06:56 Alice Marsh: recap — we will: 1) send a tailored pilot proposal and pricing sheet; 2) security pack (SOC2, data flow, KMS options); 3) benchmark plan and an example Console export; 4) propose a 2-week pilot scope with expected metrics.
07:14 Lena Park: sounds good. can we do the bench in rolling windows that include market open spikes?
07:19 Ben Ortiz: yes include your spike traces. ideally send a 2-day sample of production traffic.
07:24 Priya Iyer: who's owning the benchmark on Redwood side?
07:26 Ben Ortiz: that'll be me (ben). I'll coordinate with Samir for security.
07:30 Marcus Dutta: ownership noted.
07:32 Alice Marsh: ok we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with docs and a proposed calendar. any other questions?
07:38 RahuI Sen: (overlap) sorry rahul — will we need infra changes to our side for the pilot?
07:42 Ben Ortiz: minimal. for Hosted pilot you just provide API keys and sample traces. for Dedicated or Private simulation we might ask for a lightweight VPN peering or temporary vpc access for on-prem benchmarks.
07:54 Lena Park: thanks all.
07:56 Alice Marsh: thanks everyone. wrap up.
